```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
data <- read.delim("housing_prices.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "", comment.char = "", check.names = TRUE)
```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)


#Checking the summary, and missing val of the data
summary(data)
colSums(is.na(data)) #No missing values are found in the data.

#Converting variables into the correct structire
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Waterfront = as.factor(Waterfront),
    New.Construct = as.factor(New.Construct),
    Central.Air = as.factor(Central.Air),
    Fuel.Type = as.factor(Fuel.Type),
    Heat.Type = as.factor(Heat.Type),
    Sewer.Type = as.factor(Sewer.Type)
  )

```



```{r}
library(dplyr)

data_cleaned <- data %>%
  #Remove houses with invalid lot size
  filter(Lot.Size > 0) %>%
  #Remove old houses that has an age 0
  filter(!(Age == 0 & New.Construct == 0))

#1st problem statement:With the current housing crisis in new york state, we want to see what factors can increase housing price for a smaller lot size

summary(data_cleaned$Lot.Size)
hist(data_cleaned$Lot.Size, breaks = 30)
quantile(data_cleaned$Lot.Size, probs = c(0.25, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75))
#Result: The data is heavily right skewed, we define smaller lot size is anything below the 40 percentile

#Filter out houses with a waterfront, and erase bigger lot sizes >40%
q <- quantile(data_cleaned$Lot.Size, 0.4) 
small_lot <- data_cleaned %>%
  filter(Lot.Size < q) 

#Model Selection
M0_A <- lm(Price ~ 1, data = small_lot)
M1_A <- lm(Price ~ ., data = small_lot)

step_fwd_A  <- step(M0_A, scope = list(lower = M0_A, upper = M1_A), direction = "forward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_fwd_A)
#Result:living area, land value, bathrooms, waterfront

step_back_A <- step(M1_A, direction = "backward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_back_A)
#Result: waterfront, land value, new construction, living area, bathrooms

step_both_A <- step(M0_A, scope = list(lower = M0_A, upper = M1_A), direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_both_A)
#Result: living area, land value, bathrooms, waterfront
```

```{r}
#3rd problem statement: How much do the unchangeable factors impact housing price vs changeable?
# --- Define groups ---
unchangeable_vars <- c("Lot.Size", "Waterfront", "Age", "Land.Value")
changeable_vars   <- c("Living.Area", "Bathrooms", "Bedrooms", "Rooms",
                       "Central.Air", "New.Construct", "Heat.Type",
                       "Fuel.Type", "Fireplaces")

data_U <- data_cleaned[, c("Price", unchangeable_vars)]
data_C <- data_cleaned[, c("Price", changeable_vars)]

#--- UNCHANGEABLE VARIABLES ---
m0_U <- lm(Price ~ 1, data = data_U)
m1_U <- lm(Price ~ ., data = data_U)

#forward selection
step_fwd_U <- step(m0_U, scope = list(lower = m0_U, upper = m1_U),
                   direction = "forward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_fwd_U)

#backward selection
step_back_U <- step(m1_U, direction = "backward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_back_U)

#stepwise
step_both_U <- step(m0_U, scope = list(lower = m0_U, upper = m1_U),
                    direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_both_U)
#MOST INFLUENTIAL VARIABLES: land value, age, lot size, waterfront

# --- CHANGEABLE VARIABLES ---
m0_C <- lm(Price ~ 1, data = data_C)
m1_C <- lm(Price ~ ., data = data_C)

# Forward selection
step_fwd_C <- step(m0_C, scope = list(lower = m0_C, upper = m1_C),
                   direction = "forward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_fwd_C)

# Backward selection
step_back_C <- step(m1_C, direction = "backward", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_back_C)

# Stepwise (both)
step_both_C <- step(m0_C, scope = list(lower = m0_C, upper = m1_C),
                    direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(step_both_C)
#MOST INFLUENTIAL VARIABLES: living area, central air, bathrooms, bedrooms


comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Unchangeable_Forward", "Unchangeable_Backward", "Unchangeable_Both",
            "Changeable_Forward", "Changeable_Backward", "Changeable_Both"),
  R2 = c(summary(step_fwd_U)$r.squared,
         summary(step_back_U)$r.squared,
         summary(step_both_U)$r.squared,
         summary(step_fwd_C)$r.squared,
         summary(step_back_C)$r.squared,
         summary(step_both_C)$r.squared),
  Adj_R2 = c(summary(step_fwd_U)$adj.r.squared,
             summary(step_back_U)$adj.r.squared,
             summary(step_both_U)$adj.r.squared,
             summary(step_fwd_C)$adj.r.squared,
             summary(step_back_C)$adj.r.squared,
             summary(step_both_C)$adj.r.squared)
)

comparison
#Result: all selection methods use (forward, back, both) produced the same results within unchangable and changeable variables. 
#About 38% of the variation of house prices is explained by factors that are unchangeable (R2 = 0.38)
#About 55% of the varation of house prices is exaplained by factors that are changeable (R2 = 0.55)

```
